item.title: Agentic AI needs a science of interaction
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78879-x

Here, the authors argue that agentic AI requires a shift from evaluating individual agents alone to analyzing interaction architectures, proposing a framework that links agent interactions, collective configurations and time-dependent outcomes.
item.dc:title: Agentic AI needs a science of interaction

item.title: Addressing the 1000-h/1000-nit stability challenge in perovskite LEDs
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79298-8

Perovskite light-emitting diodes offer vivid, efficient displays, but long-term stability at practical brightness remains difficult. Yuan et al. add a fluorinated molecular layer to lower voltage, extending device life and enabling a stable flexible perovskite display.
item.dc:title: Addressing the 1000-h/1000-nit stability challenge in perovskite LEDs

item.title: Resolving phonons in superconductor Bi<sub>2</sub>Sr<sub>2</sub>CaCu<sub>2</sub>O<sub>8+δ</sub> at sub-unit-cell resolution
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77617-7

The role of phonons in cuprate superconductivity remains debated, partly because their layered structures host complex lattice dynamics. Here, sub-unit-cell spectroscopy resolves layer-localized phonons in Bi-2212 and reveals a spatial correlation between superstructure-driven phonon frequency modulations and superconducting gap variations.
item.dc:title: Resolving phonons in superconductor Bi<sub>2</sub>Sr<sub>2</sub>CaCu<sub>2</sub>O<sub>8+δ</sub> at sub-unit-cell resolution

item.title: Continuous directed evolution using engineered human B cell lines
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79127-y

This study describes the development of a continuous directed evolution platform in human B cell lines (CODE-HB) that repurposes the somatic hypermutation (SHM) mechanisms to evolve cytoplasmic reporter proteins as well as therapeutically relevant antibodies.

item.title: Decoherence resilience of the non-Hermitian skin effect
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78483-z

Decoherence, often viewed as detrimental to coherent transport, can instead enhance the non-Hermitian skin effect, which persists into the fully incoherent regime. Its effect can be tuned by the type and implementation of decoherence.
item.dc:title: Decoherence resilience of the non-Hermitian skin effect

item.title: Fe(III) hydrolysis-driven Fe(III)/Fe(IV) redox couple for iron sludge-free Fenton-like oxidation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 06 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79181-6

This study reveals that Fe(III) hydrolysis can establish the Fe(III)/Fe(IV) redox couple to activate peroxymonosulfate under neutral conditions. This enables an iron sludge-free and acid pH-independent Fenton-like process for water decontamination.
item.dc:title: Fe(III) hydrolysis-driven Fe(III)/Fe(IV) redox couple for iron sludge-free Fenton-like oxidation
